subject: physics_2
question_text: If the wavelength of electromagnetic radiation is doubled, what happens to the energy of photon?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Paper-II bank the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Hand-checked: E = hc/λ, so E ∝ 1/λ; replacing λ by 2λ gives E′ = hc/(2λ) = E/2 — doubling the wavelength halves the photon energy, matching the book's E₂ = E/2 (p.41).

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The relation E = hc/λ

lines.text: Energy of a photon: E = hc/λ

lines: Here λ is the wavelength of the radiation.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The relation must be on paper before the conclusion.
steps.why: The whole answer follows from E = hc/λ: h and c are constants, so the energy depends on the wavelength alone, as 1/λ.
common_mistakes: Writing E = hcλ. The wavelength divides, it does not multiply: E = hc/λ.
Treating E as proportional to λ. The relation is inverse — a longer wavelength must mean a smaller energy.

recall.must_convey: That photon energy is E = hc/λ, so energy is inversely proportional to wavelength.
accept: E equals h c by lambda
E proportional to one by lambda

steps.memory_tip: h and c are fixed; only λ can change, and it sits below the line.

steps.label: The energy becomes half

lines.text: When λ is doubled: E′ = hc/(2λ) = E/2

lines: So the energy of the photon becomes half.

lines.text: Doubling λ halves the photon energy

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Say half, and show where the 2 comes from.
steps.why: Replacing λ by 2λ in E = hc/λ puts the 2 in the denominator, so the new energy is E/2.
common_mistakes: Saying the energy doubles. E and λ change in opposite directions.
Answering half with no working. Write E′ = hc/(2λ) = E/2 so the relation mark is also safe.

recall.must_convey: That doubling the wavelength makes the photon energy half.

steps.memory_tip: λ up two times means E down two times — the product hc never changes.

insider_note: One mark is for E = hc/λ on paper and one for the word half — an answer with only the word half loses the relation mark.
